skill.name: api-mitmproxy
skill.description: Guide authorized mitmproxy API testing through HTTPS interception, request modification, replay, Python addons, mobile workflows, and HAR export.
skill.summary: Inspect and automate authorized API traffic testing with mitmproxy.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, educational vulnerable-code examples, and documented security references. Confirmed risks include a mutable remote script piped to Bash, third-party token access, unauthenticated all-interface proxy bindings, and destructive certificate reset guidance. Additional concerns are mutable CI action references, authorization token logging, and persistent interception CA trust.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Download a versioned release, verify its checksum, then execute the local file in a separate step.

remediation.issue: Third-party actions use mutable references and receive repository access.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every action to a reviewed commit SHA and move permissions to the smallest job scope.

remediation.issue: Proxy examples bind to every network interface.
remediation.suggestion: Default to loopback and require explicit authentication, firewall restrictions, and authorization before remote binding.

remediation.issue: Certificate reset recursively deletes all mitmproxy state.
remediation.suggestion: Back up the directory and delete only generated certificate files after explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: The addon logs part of intercepted authorization tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Remove token output or replace the complete value with a nonreversible fingerprint.

remediation.issue: Trusted interception certificates can remain installed after testing.
remediation.suggestion: Add cleanup steps for every platform and protect the mitmproxy CA private key throughout testing.

content.value_statement: API traffic is difficult to inspect, modify, and replay across clients. This skill provides structured mitmproxy workflows for authorized security testing and debugging.
actual_capabilities: Explains mitmproxy, mitmweb, and mitmdump setup for authorized API traffic inspection.
Guides recording, replaying, filtering, and exporting intercepted flows.
Provides Python addon examples for request, response, GraphQL, and WebSocket testing.
Covers regular, transparent, reverse, and upstream proxy modes.
Describes certificate installation and mobile traffic interception workflows.
Outlines CI integration and OWASP API Security Top 10 testing.
limitations: Does not include an executable mitmproxy addon or automated scanner.
Requires mitmproxy, Python 3.9 or later, and client proxy configuration.
Certificate pinning bypass depends on external tools and device access.
Users must obtain authorization and protect captured credentials, personal data, and flow files.

use_cases.title: Debug API requests
use_cases.description: Inspect requests, responses, headers, and WebSocket messages while developing an API client.

use_cases.title: Assess API controls
use_cases.description: Modify and replay authorized traffic to evaluate authentication, authorization, input validation, and business logic.

use_cases.title: Inspect mobile traffic
use_cases.description: Configure a test device, install the interception certificate, and analyze application API behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Start local inspection
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through inspecting traffic from [client] to [API] with mitmweb on loopback. Include certificate setup and safe cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Filter relevant traffic
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mitmproxy workflow that captures only [domain] and [methods], saves flows, and exports a reviewable HAR file.

prompt_templates.title: Design an addon
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python addon for authorized testing of [control]. Redact credentials, preserve original requests, and define evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an end-to-end assessment for [application]. Cover proxy architecture, mobile pinning, replay controls, OWASP tests, evidence handling, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Inspect login traffic without exposing credentials.
output: Run the proxy on loopback and configure only the test client.
Capture authentication flow metadata while fully redacting passwords, cookies, and authorization values.
Remove the interception certificate and securely delete sensitive captures after review.

output_examples.output: The plan identifies target operations, controlled identities, request variants, expected denials, captured evidence, and restoration steps.

output: Pin tools and actions to reviewed versions.
Use job-scoped credentials with minimum permissions.
Keep flow files encrypted and restrict artifact access and retention.

best_practices: Test only systems and accounts covered by written authorization.
Use isolated environments, loopback bindings, and minimum network exposure.
Redact secrets and remove trusted interception certificates after testing.
anti_patterns: Do not intercept production traffic without explicit authorization and a data-handling plan.
Do not log complete tokens, cookies, passwords, or personal data.
Do not pipe remote installers to a shell or use mutable CI action references.

faq.question: Does this skill install mitmproxy?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup commands and workflows, but you must install and manage mitmproxy in your environment.

faq.question: Can it decrypt HTTPS traffic?
faq.answer: Yes, when the authorized client trusts the mitmproxy CA and certificate pinning does not prevent interception.

faq.question: Does it support mobile applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Android and iOS proxy configuration, certificate trust, and external pinning-bypass approaches.

faq.question: Can it automate API tests?
faq.answer: It provides Python addon patterns for modifying and analyzing traffic, but the examples require adaptation before execution.

faq.question: Can it export captured traffic?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains flow recording, replay, and HAR export for later analysis and reporting.

faq.question: What authorization is required?
faq.answer: Use it only on systems, applications, devices, and accounts included in written testing authorization.
